updates.headline: v0.1.81 — District 1 Mission Flow: First Half
updates.summary: Clear the initial threat, repair communications through static and moving zones, and hold the final signal to open the gate.

categories.name: District 1 Flow
changes: CHAPTER 1: Replaced the earlier three-batch prototype with a District 1 intro, exactly ten legitimate initial kills, and a five-second post-clear beat before communications repair.

CHAPTER 1: Repair communications in a static 5×5 area from 0 to 50, then follow the same 3×3 area as it bounces within authored bounds from 50 to 100. Repair advances one point per second only while inside; leaving pauses progress.

CHAPTER 1: Authored District 1 enemy sources supply configurable repair pressure. At 100, new spawning stops and a five-second continuous hold at the final signal zone opens the existing animated gate. Surviving pressure enemies remain; ambush and door-lock recovery are future work.

categories.name: Existing Systems
changes: PRESENTATION: Reused existing objective notifications, world/minimap waypoints and contextual progress. Authored positions, HUD, cards, minimap framing, canonical combat and normal XP are preserved.

categories.name: Objective Foundation
changes: CHAPTER FOUNDATION: Added reusable objective waypoints with configurable labels, category icons, optional distance, and off-screen direction indicators. One target API drives both the world indication and the existing Chapter minimap.

CHAPTER FOUNDATION: Added reusable rectangular ObjectiveZone detection and an original floor border with subtle translucent fill. Authored footprints stay intact, jumping remains inside the taller detection area, and 5×5 zones can resize to 3×3 at runtime.

categories.name: Development Preview
changes: DEVELOPMENT: Chapter1_Blockout now provides preview actions for the authored signal and door targets, zone visibility, and zone sizes. Existing HUD, district/corridor framing, combat prototype, and gate flow remain intact; signal repair, moving zones, ambushes, door interactions, and the new District 1 mission sequence are future work.

CARDS: Bottom-left card choices now use a smaller 1.2 presentation with tighter spacing and fit beside the player HUD. Existing selection, animations, and queued offers remain intact.

categories.name: Chapter 1-1

CHAPTER 1-1: Combat remains 10 → 10 → 20, but progress now reveals cumulative targets as 0/10 → 10/20 → 20/40 → 40/40. All 40 legitimate kills still open the exit.

Only legitimate enemies owned by this encounter advance the continuous DEFEAT ENEMIES 0/40 objective. After 40/40, the two original gate walls smoothly return to their authored open transforms and the corridor is traversable.

categories.name: Developer Prototype
changes: Four outer districts form a controlled route from 1-1 through 1-4, ending at a central 1-5 arena that is nearly twice the area of the largest outer district.
Every connection is open for this layout test. The corridors are 14 units wide, with an angled final approach into the arena and no gameplay elevation.
The isolated scene uses neutral blockout geometry and a scene-only first-person walkthrough speed of 10. Existing gameplay scenes and Story progression remain unchanged.

categories.name: Story

categories.name: Story
changes: The new Chapter path tracks Missions 1-1 through 1-6 in order and waits for each mission's authored completion event before offering Continue.
Continue preserves the Chapter build and creates a mission-start checkpoint. Restart after death restores that checkpoint, while save and resume retain the current mission and build.
Existing Offline Story combat and saves continue through the legacy flow; no current Explore, Core, or Boss event completes Mission 1-1.

changes: A critical hit without Critical Damage upgrades now deals the same damage as a normal hit, while still registering and appearing as a crit.
Critical Damage upgrades retain their existing additive amounts and stacking rules, starting from 1.0×.
Crit Chance, which attacks can crit, and other starting stats are unchanged.

updates.headline: v0.1.60 — Faster Damage Popups

updates.headline: v0.1.59 — Responsive FPS Movement

categories.name: Gameplay

Jumping retains natural takeoff motion, while repeated hops and air steering stay within the effective Movement Speed limit.
Dash, jump height, gravity, and Movement Speed bonuses retain their existing behavior.

categories.name: Story
